blocks.directed: And suddenly we can use three.

blocks.text: Because these are different arrangements of the same manifested reality.
blocks.directed: Because these are different arrangements of the same manifested reality.

blocks.text: We’re not changing the ultimate nature of Śiva every time we change our classification.
blocks.directed: We’re not changing the ultimate nature of Śiva every time we change our classification.

blocks.text: In the same way, one may reason out a ninefold classification and other arrangements.
blocks.directed: In the same way, one may reason out a ninefold classification and other arrangements.

blocks.directed: Because the point isn’t to become obsessed with one particular number.

blocks.directed: The divisions have to be intelligible.

blocks.text: They must correspond to meaningful distinctions in the manner of manifestation.
blocks.directed: They must correspond to meaningful distinctions in the manner of manifestation.

blocks.text: But the same cosmic reality can be understood through different arrangements.
blocks.directed: But the same cosmic reality can be understood through different arrangements.

blocks.text: But Abhinavagupta is explicitly allowing several schemes.
blocks.directed: But Abhinavagupta is explicitly allowing several schemes.

blocks.text: The arrangement depends upon the kind of analysis being undertaken.
blocks.directed: The arrangement depends upon the kind of analysis being undertaken.

blocks.text: The divisions are instruments of understanding, not independent ultimate realities.
blocks.directed: The divisions are instruments of understanding, not independent ultimate realities.

blocks.directed: And now comes the climax of the chapter.

blocks.text: Because we’re going to take absolutely everything we’ve learned and show why there are six great cosmic pathways.

11. The six adhvans — three ways of being an object
Right.
blocks.directed:

blocks.text: We’re finally going to explain how they fit together.
blocks.directed: We’re finally going to explain how they fit together.

blocks.directed: First, three belong to the domain of the knowable.

blocks.text: The path of the great divisions.
blocks.directed: The path of the great divisions.

blocks.text: Because the objective side of manifestation can be considered in three modes.
blocks.directed: Because the objective side of manifestation can be considered in three modes.

Sthūla — gross.
Sūkṣma — subtle.
Para — supreme or higher.
So the same objective manifestation is considered through increasingly comprehensive levels.

blocks.text: Then the principles pervading those worlds.
blocks.directed: Then the principles pervading those worlds.

blocks.directed: Then the kalās encompassing collections of principles.

blocks.directed: A world is a particular domain of manifestation.

blocks.directed: A tattva is a common principle running through worlds.

blocks.directed: And a kalā is a higher unity running through groups of tattvas.

blocks.directed: So we’re not talking about three completely different universes.

blocks.text: We’re examining one universe at three degrees of generality.
blocks.directed: We’re examining one universe at three degrees of generality.

blocks.directed: It’s like looking at a book.

blocks.text: You can examine a particular sentence.
blocks.directed: You can examine a particular sentence.

blocks.text: Then the grammar through which sentences are structured.
blocks.directed: Then the grammar through which sentences are structured.

blocks.text: Then the more comprehensive organisation through which language becomes meaningful.
blocks.directed: Then the more comprehensive organisation through which language becomes meaningful.

blocks.text: But now we turn toward the knowing subject.
blocks.directed: But now we turn toward the knowing subject.

Now Abhinavagupta says that through repose in the knowing subject:

blocks.text: The same manifestation can be understood through another threefold distinction.

Pada-adhvan.
blocks.directed:
Pada — articulation through the means of knowing
Pada-adhvan.

blocks.text: The condition of being a means of knowing.
blocks.directed: The condition of being a means of knowing.

blocks.text: Now, pada can mean an articulated word, expression, or meaningful linguistic unit.
blocks.directed: Now, pada can mean an articulated word, expression, or meaningful linguistic unit.

blocks.text: And ordinary linguistic articulation involves differentiation.
blocks.directed: And ordinary linguistic articulation involves differentiation.

blocks.text: The structure of language permits different meanings to be expressed and known.

blocks.text: But in this tantric analysis, pada isn’t merely a dictionary category.

blocks.directed: It’s the pathway in which the expressive power of consciousness is functioning through differentiated cognition.

blocks.text: The means of knowledge is active.
blocks.directed: The means of knowledge is active.

blocks.directed: Now imagine you’re investigating some complicated Sanskrit passage.

blocks.directed: The differentiated cognitive operation is extraordinarily active.

blocks.directed: That’s a useful illustration of this level.

Mantra-adhvan.
blocks.directed:
Mantra — the waves begin to settle
Mantra-adhvan.

blocks.text: When the waves of agitation belonging to the means of knowledge are becoming pacified.
blocks.directed: When the waves of agitation belonging to the means of knowledge are becoming pacified.

blocks.directed: Because we’ve encountered this imagery already.

blocks.directed: And now, the waves of the knowing instrument itself.

blocks.directed: So the mantra pathway is connected with the settling of the differentiated cognitive activity.

blocks.directed: Now imagine a mantra that you’ve learned.

blocks.directed: At first you’re intensely concerned with pronunciation.

blocks.text: With where one sound begins and another ends.
blocks.directed: With where one sound begins and another ends.

blocks.text: But as contemplation deepens, those differentiated operations can become increasingly unified.
blocks.directed: But as contemplation deepens, those differentiated operations can become increasingly unified.

blocks.text: The mantra is no longer merely a sequence of separately apprehended sounds.
blocks.directed: The mantra is no longer merely a sequence of separately apprehended sounds.

blocks.directed: Now, that’s an illustration, not a claim that Abhinavagupta gives a full japa instruction in this sentence.

blocks.directed: He’s defining the pathway in terms of the calming of cognition.

blocks.directed: And then comes the final one.

blocks.text: And now the agitations of cognition have subsided.
blocks.directed: And now the agitations of cognition have subsided.

blocks.text: The completeness of the knowing subject.
blocks.directed: The completeness of the knowing subject.

blocks.text: The ultimate knower isn’t an isolated little individual.
blocks.directed: The ultimate knower isn’t an isolated little individual.

blocks.text: It’s consciousness resting in the bliss of its own freedom.
blocks.directed: It’s consciousness resting in the bliss of its own freedom.

blocks.text: And here the phonemic pathway is understood through that fullness.
blocks.directed: And here the phonemic pathway is understood through that fullness.

blocks.text: Because we began with language as something that articulates distinct meanings.
blocks.directed: Because we began with language as something that articulates distinct meanings.

blocks.text: Then mantra as the calming of cognitive differentiation.
blocks.directed: Then mantra as the calming of cognitive differentiation.

blocks.directed: And now varṇa as related to the fully awakened knowing subject.

blocks.directed: And Abhinavagupta says that through repose in this fullness, the reality attains its own essential nature.

blocks.directed: Having obtained or recovered its own nature.

blocks.directed: And what exactly has been moving through these stages?

blocks.directed: Three modes in which its expressive power is understood.

blocks.text: And now the entire chapter comes together.

13. The punchline — there are six pathways, but only one reality
Right.
blocks.directed:
13. The punchline — there are six pathways, but only one reality
Right.

blocks.text: On the expressive and subjective side:

blocks.directed: Varṇa — phonemic power resting in full knowership

blocks.text: It’s appropriate that one and the same reality should be sixfold.
blocks.directed: It’s appropriate that one and the same reality should be sixfold.

blocks.directed: Because we’ve spent ten chapters examining an absolutely enormous array of distinctions.

blocks.directed: And here Abhinavagupta is saying that the very division of manifestation into six cosmic pathways doesn’t compromise its fundamental unity.

blocks.directed: But all six are ways in which one reality manifests itself.

blocks.directed: And it’s that one reality that finally rests in its own nature.

blocks.text: The entire universe becomes intelligible through a structured series of distinctions.
blocks.directed: The entire universe becomes intelligible through a structured series of distinctions.

blocks.directed: Yet the distinctions themselves don’t establish six independent worlds.

blocks.text: And that manifestation isn’t independent of the conscious freedom of Śiva.
blocks.directed: And that manifestation isn’t independent of the conscious freedom of Śiva.

blocks.text: So now the whole cosmological part of our discussion has acquired a new purpose.
blocks.directed: So now the whole cosmological part of our discussion has acquired a new purpose.

blocks.directed: The six adhvans aren’t merely abstract classifications.

blocks.text: They’re going to become essential in the practices of purification and initiation.
blocks.directed: They’re going to become essential in the practices of purification and initiation.

blocks.directed: And when we come to the initiation chapters, you’ll see why it was so important to establish the cosmic pathways first.

blocks.text: Because in those rituals, the practitioner is not merely receiving some arbitrary ceremonial blessing.
blocks.directed: Because in those rituals, the practitioner is not merely receiving some arbitrary ceremonial blessing.

14. The three concluding Āryā verses
These three verses occur at the close of Chapter 10 in the Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism edition. They are also independently attested in Tantrāloka 11.51–53. They summarise the numbers of worlds, principles, phonemes, mantras and padas associated with the kalās. Sanskrit &

blocks.text: Padamantravarṇam ekaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ dhareti ca nivṛttiḥ.

blocks.text: Then Pratiṣṭhā gets twenty-three tattvas, twenty-three phonemes, fifty-six worlds, five mantras and five padas.
blocks.directed: Then Pratiṣṭhā gets twenty-three tattvas, twenty-three phonemes, fifty-six worlds, five mantras and five padas.

blocks.directed: Now, why does he say agni-nayana?

blocks.directed: Because he’s encoding numbers through symbolic words.

blocks.text: And in this mnemonic arrangement, they give twenty-three.
blocks.directed: And in this mnemonic arrangement, they give twenty-three.

blocks.text: Then rasa — six — and śara — five — give fifty-six.
blocks.directed: Then rasa — six — and śara — five — give fifty-six.

blocks.text: So Abhinavagupta is using Sanskrit numerical wordplay to pack enormous amounts of information into a tiny metrical space.
blocks.directed: So Abhinavagupta is using Sanskrit numerical wordplay to pack enormous amounts of information into a tiny metrical space.

blocks.text: It’s like creating a mnemonic spreadsheet.
blocks.directed: It’s like creating a mnemonic spreadsheet.

blocks.text: And the fourth, Śāntā, is summarised in this mnemonic as three tattvas, three phonemes, one mantra, one pada and eighteen worlds.
blocks.directed: And the fourth, Śāntā, is summarised in this mnemonic as three tattvas, three phonemes, one mantra, one pada and eighteen worlds.

blocks.text: There’s a textual subtlety here: the prose explicitly assigns four tattvas to Śāntā, from Śuddhavidyā through Śakti, whereas the closing mnemonic says three. The discrepancy appears in the transmitted text and should not be silently harmonised.

And now we’ve arrived at an important turning point in the Tantrasāra.
